transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-09
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~75 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Liam O'Connor, Priya Kapoor, Noah Patel, Avery Brooks, Diego Marin, Sasha Liu, Camille Turner

Summary: polish pitch, align on competitive messaging, demo flow practice, assign owners

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya: All right everyone, thanks for jumping on. quick internal session, gonna keep it very tactical. we've got about an hour plus in case we go over.
[00:17] Avery: yep, thanks Maya. we've been getting more questions on dedicated vs hosted, and some reps are, like, struggling with the one-liner.
[00:27] Liam: mm-hmm. hello all, i'll take the technical bits. also want to practice the demo handoff to avoid the awkward pause where we talk about kv cache and then the customer zones out.
[00:40] Diego: real talk — trainers want a clean 2-minute pitch to teach. not 10 slides.
[00:47] Maya: agreed. i'm going to read the current 2-min and we riff. here goes: "Redwood Inference is a developer-first platform for running and optimizing LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. We make inference predictable and economical with a unified runtime, smart routing, and tooling for observability and rollouts."
[01:12] Speaker 1 (Sasha?): that's pretty crisp but it's heavy. folks ask for an immediate why — like "why choose you vs just run it on cloud?"
[01:23] Maya: good — so second sentence should be the benefit: "We reduce per-token cost and stabilize latency so product teams don't have to babysit inference infra."
[01:34] Noah: drop in numbers when possible, like typical p95 latency or percent cost savings — but careful to not promise exacts.
[01:44] Liam: we can say "often 20-40% lower unit cost via batching, caching, and quantization profiles" — that frames it. but watch phrasing: customers will ask for benchmarks.
[01:56] Diego: also need a one-liner on security for enterprise — "private deployments with KMS and audit logs" or similar. some reps just say 'we do security' and it sounds weak.
[02:06] Maya: ok draft: "Redwood helps product teams ship LLM features faster with predictable latency and lower inference cost, and for regulated workloads we offer private deployments with KMS, audit logs, and SSO."
[02:20] Avery: solid. can we add a quick line about rollback/fallback? customers like reliability stories — "graceful degradation with automatic fallbacks".
[02:31] Liam: yes — briefly: "we automatically fallback to compatible model variants and regions to keep apps online during capacity events." maybe too long.
[02:41] Maya: note to self, shorten but capture the idea.

[03:05] (ROLEPLAY)
[03:05] Maya: Avery, you're the buyer. i'm the AE. go.
[03:08] Avery: hi — we're building a customer support assistant, latency's a big deal. what do you offer?
[03:12] Maya: absolutely — short: we provide a low-latency runtime and tooling to control cost. customers that move from raw endpoints to our Dedicated or optimized Hosted profiles typically see fewer latency spikes and lower token cost.
[03:23] Avery: Hmm, how do you compare to Anthropic/OpenAI?
[03:27] Liam: (interrupt) quick note — we don't compare model capabilities; we compare serving economics and reliability. say: "we don't change the model's reasoning, we change how it's served so your product is stable and predictable."
[03:38] Avery: the buyer pushes: "we already use model-hosting on cloud, why add Redwood?"
[03:42] Maya: reply: "If your team is iterating fast, you want predictable p95 latency, cheaper average per-token cost, and rollout tools so your experiments don't create customer-visible regressions. otherwise teams spend a lot of cycles troubleshooting infra and model regressions."
[03:58] Sasha: little filler phrase: leads want 'no-ops' or 'low-ops' language sometimes — be careful with 'no-ops' because it's not true. say 'minimal ops' or 'managed inference'.
[04:09] Liam: also be prepared for the security heavyweight — customers will ask SOC2, SSO/SAML, HSM/KMS. have those bullets ready.

[04:35] Maya: switching to demo handoff: Liam, you do the technical demo after the AE intro. what's the 90-second tech narrative?
[04:42] Liam: 1) architecture sketch: model variants + routing layer, 2) performance levers: batching, kv cache, quant profiles, 3) observability: p95 breakdown, per-route cost. keep each point super short.
[04:56] Camille: trainers want exact demo transitions: AE says customer problem and success criteria, then SE says what metric they'll demo. e.g., 'we'll show p95 latency for 4 second scenarios' — concrete metrics.
[05:08] Maya: roleplay the handoff now. i'll intro.
[05:12] Maya: "...so latency is critical, we aim for under 200ms p95 for chat contexts. Liam will show how routing and caching help with that."
[05:20] Liam: "thanks Maya — quick architecture view..." (demo choreography continues)

[05:55] Diego: small note — some transcripts in calls call the product 'Red wood' or 'Redwood Private' and reps need to enunciate the product lines consistently: Redwood Hosted, Redwood Dedicated, Redwood Private.

[06:10] Avery: objections — cost. buyers ask 'is dedicated expensive?' practice answer?
[06:14] Liam: say: 'Dedicated gives predictable throughput and often lower cost at scale; Hosted is best for quick time-to-value and bursty usage. we also offer autoscaling and burst capacity to mitigate spikes.'
[06:26] Maya: add example: "If you're doing sustained high qps, Dedicated at committed capacity often reduces unit cost; for variable workloads, Hosted with smart routing is cheaper overall."

[06:45] Noah: competitive tactics: when competitor claims "we're simpler" — pivot to what matters: "simpler isn't cheaper at scale, and it doesn't buy you observability for regressions."
[06:58] Diego: for OpenAI comparisons, reps should avoid capability claims and emphasize 'serving layer' benefits. use examples of rollout (canary, automatic fallback) to show reliability differentiator.

[07:20] (TRANSCRIPTION GLITCH)
[07:20] Speaker 2: (inaudible) -- "...quantiza...tion profiles, uh, save, sais..."

[07:34] Maya: let's practice a tough buyer — privacy/regulation; 60-second answer.
[07:39] Sasha: 'We support private deployments with a customer-controlled control plane, on-prem options, VPC peering, and integrations with KMS/HSM for encryption of keys at rest. We also provide audit logs and SSO.'
[07:53] Avery: follow-up: do you support air-gapped?
[07:56] Liam: yes, we have an on-prem package for highly regulated workloads — need solutions team and security review, but it's doable.

[08:10] Maya: good. now demo practice — quick walkthrough of the console view showing per-route latency and cost; Liam you'll narrate.
[08:18] Liam: narrating: "here's route X, p95 180ms, per-token cost $0.00x, we're able to reduce tail latencies by prefix caching, and rollout policy shows canary at 5% then 20%."
[08:33] Camille: trainers: call out the 'how to demo' script: 1) set context 2) show metric 3) explain how it maps to buyer impact 4) propose trial/pilot.

[08:47] (Pressure test)
[08:47] Avery: buyer: "what if my TPR is 99.9%?" (misspoke: meant SLO)
[08:51] Maya: clarify question — "do you mean SLO or availability?" small teachable moment — correct the buyer wording and explain SLOs.

[09:12] Roleplay continues for ~20 minutes with different reps. excerpts:
[09:12] Maya: "we often recommend starting with a small pilot on Hosted with a dedicated profile and then moving to Dedicated if throughput and cost justify it."
[09:22] Diego: "Make sure to ask about timelines and who's the technical owner — that drives whether to recommend Hosted or Dedicated."

[18:30] (MID-CALL RECAP)
[18:30] Maya: recap: 1) tighten the 2-min pitch, 2) prepare security bullets, 3) assemble benchmark slide, 4) demo choreography clarified. owners?
[18:40] Priya: i'll own the playbook updates and competitor one-pager.
[18:45] Liam: i'll do the benchmark slide.
[18:48] Maya: i'll update the pitch and final slide. Camille will book roleplay sessions.

[19:05] (DEEP DIVE — COMPETITIVE TABLE TALK)
[19:05] Noah: quick table: competitor claim vs rebuttal. example: 'Competitor: simpler API' rebuttal: 'We provide a unified runtime that reduces ops time and gives predictable economics.'
[19:23] Diego: add a 'trap' list — things not to say: don't say 'we're better model' or 'our models are smarter' — that invites capability debates.

[25:00] (TRANSCRIPT NOTE: some speaker labels wrong below)
[25:07] Speaker 3: "...we've got customers who moved from raw endpoints and reduced cost by around 30% over 6 months, but results vary."
[25:20] Maya: okay that stat is useful but we should prefer 'typical' language or 'customers often see' to avoid exact promises.

[30:10] (OBJECTION PRACTICE)
[30:10] Avery: buyer: "I can self-host, why pay you?"
[30:14] Liam: "Self-hosting requires ops bandwidth — our value is operational expertise: kernel selection, batching, KV cache tuning, and automated fallback during capacity events. those are time sinks for product teams."
[30:30] Maya: also mention the support/SLAs and playbook we bring for production incidents.

[40:00] (SHOW & TELL: QUICK SLIDE REVIEW)
[40:00] Maya: walkthrough of the proposed updated slide. (reads slide)
[40:12] Diego: suggestion — add an 'elevator objection response' box on slide 2 with 3 short rebuttals.
[40:21] Priya: will add to playbook.

[48:00] (FINAL ROLEPLAY)
[48:00] Maya: final 5-min run-through.
[48:05] Maya (AE): "We're Redwood Inference. We help engineering teams run LLM features with predictable latency and lower unit cost. For regulated workloads we offer private deployments with KMS and audit logs. Can you tell me your success criteria?"
[48:20] Avery (buyer): "We need sub-250ms p95 and a solid audit trail; timeline is Q4."
[48:27] Liam (SE): "Great, here's a short plan: pilot on Hosted with a dedicated profile to validate latency, measure p95 under real traffic, then move to Dedicated for committed capacity if cost benefits align. we'll instrument with per-route tracing and rollback policies in case of regressions."
[48:45] Avery: "Sounds good. price?"
[48:49] Maya: "We'll follow up with pricing and a pilot plan. Priya will share playbook and security docs."

[49:10] (CLOSING)
[49:10] Maya: quick recap of owners (see action items). any other questions?
[49:18] Camille: i'll coordinate roleplay invites for next week.
[49:22] Diego: i'll draft the competitive one-pager bullets and send to Priya.
[49:28] Priya: sounds good.
[49:32] Maya: thanks everyone. end of session.

--- End transcript ---

Notes: there's a few inaudible lines and one short glitch around quantization phrasing; the team agreed clear owners and dates for collateral updates.
